system_prompt_style.evidence_quote: All threads are provided the same few-shot prompt for every step of the problem completion. Thus, THREAD only requires generating a single prompt for a given setting.
system_prompt_style.note: One fixed few-shot prompt q prepended to each thread's context; per-benchmark prompt files.

env_context_strategy.evidence_quote: This prompt,q, is prepended to the context for each thread,G(q +c +Y ), forming the full context from which the thread will generate.
env_context_strategy.note: No repository/env context injection; agent acts in text environments (ALFWorld/WebShop/TextCraft).

context_compaction.evidence_quote: Child threads return only the information (tokens) needed for the parent to complete its work.
context_compaction.note: Compaction is via spawning: child work is replaced in the parent context by the child's print() output (ψ).

tool_call_format.evidence_quote: we leverage the coding-based skills of the model to define variables that represent pieces of information that are important for the given problem
tool_call_format.note: Actions are emitted as text lines beginning with '>' followed by the => listen token; environment-specific command syntax (e.g. search[...], click[...]).

tool_count.note: No tool schema list; actions are free-text environment commands.

edit_primitive.evidence_quote: THREAD frames model generation as an execution thread that, given the context, can run to completion or spawn new threads.

tool_schema_source.evidence_quote: The few-shot examples are comprised in a single prompt with examples of successful spawning and problem solving at different thread depths

protocol_standardization.evidence_quote: THREAD can be implemented with the same few-shot prompt used for every thread at every step of the task completion.

loop_primitives.evidence_quote: They simply generate tokens that represent the action and then produce the token ωlisten to listen for feedback from the environment.

planning_granularity.evidence_quote: Instead of outlining a full plan and attempting all steps, THREAD involves specifying one step, allocating this to a child thread, and receiving feedback from the child thread before proceeding.

multi_agent_topology.evidence_quote: a parent thread waits for the execution of the child to complete before proceeding
